items.title: Jerry Blumberg Interview, 1961-04-15
items.q: we used to stand behind the piano when he was playing with Bunk and, and just listen to the piano.

ctx.x: Yeah. And who is Don Ewell?

Well, he's a piano player from Baltimore, uh, plays many, well, he has a way, uh, a style which, uh, uh, uses many of the stylisms, uh, uh, from the jazz tradition. And, and, uh, at that particular time, uh, he was very much on a jelly kick, and, and, uh, we used to stand behind the piano when he was playing with Bunk and, and just listen to the piano. He was playing beautiful jelly roll style piano.
And, uh, uh, well, specifically in the ensemble, what kind of thing would he be doing?

items.title: Jerry Blumberg Interview, 1961-04-06
items.q: Oh, yeah, I came up to hear the band with Don, and that was very exciting, too, because Don was playing exceptionally well with the band

ctx.x: I didn't move up, I think, until after the second one was over. The second one, when Don was there.

Yeah. Did you get up to hear the band with Don? Oh, yeah, I came up to hear the band with Don, and that was very exciting, too, because Don was playing exceptionally well with the band, and Kratka and I and a few others used to stand behind the piano there and just listen to the piano, which was very exciting, some very exciting Jelly Roll style.
Yeah, Don was playing more Jelly Roll style then than he does now.
